Not with deep cleaning.⁠
Not with organizing.⁠
Not with catching up.⁠
Start with a simple rhythm.⁠
⁠
The Clean Mama Routine shows you exactly:⁠
⁠
✔️what to do daily⁠

⁠

cleaning.⁠
Comment GUIDE and I’ll send it to you or grab it at cleanmama.com/subscribe.⁠
Small tasks + a clear plan = less deciding⁠

I haven’t had to decide when to wash my sheets and towels in over 20 years.
That might sound like a small thing, but it’s actually one of the biggest reasons the Clean Mama Routine works.
When you assign a Weekly Task to a specific day, you stop relying on memory, motivation, or guessing.

You don’t have to wonder: Did I wash the sheets last week? How many times have these towels been used?

You already know.
That’s one less decision to make, and one more thing your routine handles for you.
The goal isn’t to create more rules.
It’s to create a simple rhythm that makes caring for your home feel easier.

✔️Comment GUIDE and I’ll send you my free Homekeeping Guide with the Daily and Weekly Tasks so you can experience how much calmer homekeeping feels when the decisions are already made.

Friday might be the most important day in the Clean Mama Routine. Not because I clean more, because I finish the week with intention.

Friday is Catch-All Day - it’s the day I take care of the little things that didn’t get done, put things back where they belong, and reset my home before the weekend begins.

That simple habit changes how my weekends feel. Instead of waking up on Saturday already behind, I wake up knowing my home is ready for whatever the weekend brings.

✨That’s what the Clean Mama Routine is all about: creating a simple rhythm that keeps your home manageable and gives you back the time and mental space to enjoy your life.

✔️ Comment GUIDE and I’ll send you my free Homekeeping Guide with the Daily and Weekly Tasks so you can start creating that same rhythm in your own home.

Thursday is Floor Washing Day...and it’s not because my floors need it.
Most people wait until something looks dirty before they clean it.
I don’t.

By Thursday, the bathrooms are done, the dusting is finished, and the vacuuming is complete. Washing the floors is simply the last step in the Weekly Tasks.

That’s what makes the Clean Mama Routine different.

You’re not reacting to the mess—you’re following a simple rhythm that keeps your home manageable without spending your weekends catching up.

✨The goal isn’t perfection. It’s consistency.

✔️Comment GUIDE and I’ll send you my free Homekeeping Guide with the Daily and Weekly Tasks. It’s the same routine I’ve used for years to keep my home running with less stress and fewer decisions.

Wednesday is Vacuum Day—and it’s more intentional than you might think.
Vacuuming isn’t just about keeping your floors clean, it’s the next step after Dusting Day.

By dusting on Tuesday and vacuuming on Wednesday, you’re working with your home instead of cleaning the same areas over and over again.
That’s the difference between having a cleaning schedule and having a system.

When the order is already decided, there’s less second-guessing, less overwhelm, and fewer decisions to make.

✔️Comment GUIDE and I’ll send you my free Homekeeping Guide with the Daily and Weekly Tasks. You’ll also get my Sunday Reset email every week with simple tips to help your home feel calmer and more manageable.

Dusting Day isn’t just about dust.
The Weekly Tasks aren’t just a checklist—they’re designed to work together.

Tuesday comes before Vacuum Day for a reason. When you dust, everything falls downward. By dusting first and vacuuming the next day, you’re working with your home instead of cleaning the same surfaces twice.

The order isn’t random. It’s intentional.

✨That’s what I love about the Clean Mama Routine. You don’t have to wonder what to clean next or second-guess yourself. The decisions have already been made, so you can spend less time thinking about cleaning and more time living your life. 

✨You’re not just dusting today—you’re preparing your home for tomorrow.

Most people don’t struggle because they hate cleaning. They struggle because they’re making thousands of tiny decisions every week.

✨ Should I clean the bathroom today? ✨ Can it wait another day? ✨ When was the last time I cleaned it?

Monday- Bathroom Day eliminates all of those decisions.

One task. One day. Done.

That’s how the Clean Mama Routine works.

⁠
Try a task or two or all of them...⁠

I don’t wash my sheets on Saturdays because Saturdays are magical.

I do it because I don’t want to think about it.
Every week, the same task happens on the same day. No reminders. No wondering how long it’s been. No decision fatigue.

That’s the real magic of the Clean Mama Routine. It removes hundreds of tiny decisions so your home keeps moving without relying on motivation.
Today’s task? Fresh sheets and towels.

🗓️Save this as your reminder—or better yet, make Saturday your sheet day too.

What if the secret isn't cleaning more...but deciding less?⁠
⁠
The biggest changes in my home didn't come from buying more organizers or spending entire weekends cleaning. They came from creating simple systems for the things I do every single day.⁠
⁠
✨ A place for the mail.⁠
✨ A routine for laundry.⁠
✨ A landing spot for keys and shoes.⁠
✨ A Sunday reset.⁠
⁠
Each one removes a few more decisions from my day, and together they make my home feel calmer, easier to manage, and so much less overwhelming.⁠
⁠
Isn’t that the real goal?⁠
Not a perfect home.⁠
A home that works for you.⁠
